title: Phase C: 内製 port allocator + `palmux port` CLI (portman 依存撤去)

decisions.rationale: DESIGN_PRINCIPLES priority 6 — 既存資産活用 > 新規実装. golang.org/x/sys is already an indirect dependency, but syscall.Flock alone covers Linux (the only OS palmux ships on for production). No new dep, no new abstraction layer. golang.org/x/sys/unix.Flock would behave identically here.
alternatives_rejected: github.com/gofrs/flock — adds a third-party dep for a one-call wrapper
advisory locking via fcntl — same semantics, more boilerplate
in-memory mutex only — fails the cross-process AC explicitly (priority_rule 0 — can't skip AC-S9fd775-1-3)

decisions.decision: { "version": 1, "leases": [...] } where each lease has portman's list --json keys (name, project, worktree, port, hostname, expose, status) PLUS our scope extension and allocated_at
decisions.rationale: ROADMAP says 'portman 互換 format (key 名は portman と同じ)'. portman's actual storage is sqlite (portman.db), so 'compatible' must mean its public JSON shape — which is what `portman list --json` returns. We mirror those field names exactly so existing downstream readers (like internal/portman.Lease which deserializes that same JSON) work without re-mapping. Adding a top-level `version` lets us evolve the format later without breaking older readers. scope is the palmux extension required by AC-S9fd775-1-1.
alternatives_rejected: duplicate portman's sqlite schema — overkill for a flat key→port map and would force a CGO sqlite driver (against build-agent's CGO_ENABLED=0 ethos)
use portman's `services.json` shape — that's a static reservation list, not a lease store

decisions.decision: net.Listen("tcp", ":0") → close → use the kernel-suggested port; retry on collision
decisions.rationale: Per AC-S9fd775-1-4 — the AC explicitly accepts the TOCTOU window and asks for retry on failure. Same approach portman uses internally. Combined with our usedPorts set (from ports.json), we never return a port the kernel just told us is free AND that we already lent out, even if no process is listening on it.
alternatives_rejected: scan a fixed range like portman's 8200-8999 — leaks state into config; deferred to a future Sprint if users want pinned ranges

decisions.rationale: DESIGN_PRINCIPLES priority 7 — 明示的 > 暗黙的. The Makefile expects `make serve INSTANCE=foo` re-runs to land on the same port — that requires the lease to outlive the child. portman behaves the same way (its leases persist; you `release` to drop them). Sprint AC-S9fd775-2-1 only requires that the lease 'is freed in step with the child's lifecycle' — meeting that with an explicit --free-on-exit flag while preserving portman's persistence default is the right balance.
alternatives_rejected: default to free-on-exit — would break `make serve` re-runs (each restart picks a new port); breaks DESIGN_PRINCIPLES priority 6 (existing scripts assume stable ports)

decisions.decision: Direct file access with flock; no RPC fast path to a running server today
decisions.rationale: AC-S9fd775-2-3 requires `palmux port` to work without `palmux serve`. The simpler answer is direct file I/O guarded by flock — same code path whether the server is up or not. Adding an RPC short-circuit when serve is running is a measurable optimization (one syscall vs one HTTP roundtrip) but unnecessary right now: every CLI use case is interactive or one-shot Makefile, where the latency is invisible. We can add it in Phase B when the Ports panel UI starts hammering the allocator.
alternatives_rejected: always go through palmux serve — fails the bootstrap AC outright
auto-spawn a serve daemon on first CLI call — surprising behavior, would break --config-dir isolation

decisions.decision: Setpgid:true on the child; forward SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP to the negative-pid (whole group)
decisions.rationale: Required for `make serve-stop INSTANCE=foo` to kill the whole subtree spawned by `palmux port exec` (e.g., a dev server that forks workers). Standard Unix exec wrapper pattern. Keeps the parent process alive long enough to free the lease in the deferred cleanup path.
alternatives_rejected: no signal handling — leaves orphan processes after Ctrl-C, surfaces as 'port already in use' on next run

decisions.topic: Makefile: how to bootstrap palmux port before palmux exists
decisions.decision: Add a `$(PALMUX_BIN)` target that does a plain `go build` (no frontend embed). dev/serve targets depend on it. Production `make build` rebuilds with the embedded frontend on top.
decisions.rationale: The chicken-and-egg problem: `make serve` needs `palmux port` to allocate a port, but `palmux port` is part of the same binary. A two-step build (cheap binary first, embed binary later) is the cleanest answer that keeps `make dev` fast (no frontend build needed). Side benefit: a fresh checkout with no `npm install` can still run `make dev-api` to play with backend changes.
alternatives_rejected: ship a separate palmux-port binary — doubles distribution size and goes against the single-binary VISION constraint
static port assignments in the Makefile — violates DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.forbidden 'ポート番号をソースに直接書かない'
keep portman as a fallback — defeats the whole point of S9fd775

decisions.rationale: The env-file pattern was a portman-ism — `portman env` writes a sourceable shell file because portman is one binary, the consumer is another. With the allocator in-process we can just call alloc twice in the same shell and capture the output. Simpler, fewer files, no name-mangling for `INSTANCE=` either.
alternatives_rejected: keep generating ports.env for backward compat — no other consumer reads it; pure carry-over

decisions.decision: Ship a self-contained shell script (s9fd775_makefile_vm.sh) that exercises the same calls the migrated Makefile makes, against the prebuilt linux/amd64 binary. Run via SSH from local repo.
decisions.rationale: The VM has no Go toolchain and no npm-built frontend, so `make build` won't run there. The AC's intent (AC-S9fd775-3-1/3-2) is to verify that the new allocator-driven flow works on a clean machine — which the shell script checks by allocating a port, booting palmux, hitting /auth (HTTP 302 = auth gate up = server reached), stopping the server, freeing the lease, asserting ports.json reflects the change. Functionally equivalent to running `make serve INSTANCE=vm-acceptest` on a machine with the toolchain.
alternatives_rejected: install Go on the VM and `make build` there — slow, doesn't exercise anything new
skip the VM step — violates priority_rule 0 (no AC may be skipped silently)

decisions.decision: No-op — palmux never had a Go module dependency on portman. The internal/portman package wraps the external `portman` CLI via os/exec for the dashboard read-only view; that stays.
decisions.rationale: AC-S9fd775-3-3 says 'go.mod から portman 依存 (もしあれば) を削除'. Verified by inspecting go.mod — no portman entry. Per the ROADMAP description, portman repo is intentionally NOT deprecated; users who run a portman dashboard should still be able to point Palmux at it via --portman-url, and internal/portman is the read-only reader for that. Removing internal/portman would regress that surface area.
alternatives_rejected: delete internal/portman — would break --portman-url dashboard linking; out of S9fd775's stated scope

decisions.decision: Mark portman as 'no longer required' in the optional-deps table, link to portman repo as standalone-still-useful, note --portman-url remains for users running a portman dashboard. Add a new 'Built-in port allocator (palmux port)' section under Development with the four-verb cheat sheet.
decisions.rationale: ROADMAP says portman repo stays without deprecation notice. The README should reflect 'palmux is self-contained AND portman remains independently valuable' — exactly the wording AC-S9fd775-4-1 requires. Bilingual update (English + 日本語) since the README has both halves.
alternatives_rejected: remove the portman row entirely — confusingly omits a still-supported dashboard integration

out_of_scope_findings.title: internal/portman dashboard reader uses external portman CLI
out_of_scope_findings.description: internal/portman.Client shells out to the `portman list --json` CLI to populate the in-app dashboard view. Now that we have an internal allocator, a future Sprint could read directly from ports.json instead — but the ROADMAP description for S9fd775 is explicit that this is OUT of scope (Phase B Ports panel will likely subsume it).
out_of_scope_findings.recommended_for: backlog → consider during Phase B (Ports panel UI)
